title: gateway: add RBAC v2 authz middleware (deny-by-default) + standardized 403s
author: Amara Diallo
release_notes: Gateway now supports RBAC v2 permission enforcement behind a feature flag. When enabled, requests to protected routes without required permissions return a standardized 403 payload with a stable error code and request_id.
content: ## Summary This PR adds authorization middleware to the API Gateway to enforce RBAC v2 permissions with deny-by-default semantics and standardized error responses. The middleware runs early in the request lifecycle and evaluates (subject, action, scope) against the policy evaluator client. Protected endpoints must declare required permissions; if they do not, the gateway will deny the request by default (with a narrowly scoped allowlist for truly public/auth-free routes). This is the first enforcement point for RBAC v2 and is designed to support a staged rollout (shadow/log-only -> enforce) to avoid denial spikes during migration. ## Motivation / context Enterprise prospects for Dedicated/Private require provable enforcement and predictable errors for “permission denied”. We currently rely on a mix of service-level checks and ad-hoc gateway rules. This introduces drift, inconsistent 403 payloads, and gaps where endpoints ship without explicit authorization constraints. This PR establishes a consistent gateway-side pattern: endpoints declare required permissions; middleware enforces them; errors and metrics are standardized. ## Design highlights - Deny-by-default: If a route is tagged as protected but missing permission metadata, we deny with RBAC_MISSING_ROUTE_PERMISSION rather than allowing “by accident”. - Explicit public allowlist: /healthz, /readyz, and the auth bootstrap endpoints remain unauthenticated/unauthorized (existing behavior) and are explicitly listed. - Feature flags: - RBAC_V2_GATEWAY_AUTHZ_MODE = off | shadow | enforce (default: off). - Shadow mode logs decisions + emits metrics but does not block. - Standardized error semantics: All authz denials return 403 with a stable error code, message, and request_id. The response is intentionally non-leaky by default; detailed reasoning stays in logs/metrics for now. - Observability: Emits counters and latency histograms for (decision, route, permission, org_id presence, cache_hit if available). Also includes structured log fields to correlate with audit logging work in later PRs. ## User-visible behavior (when enabled) - Missing/invalid authn still returns existing 401/403 behavior (unchanged). - Authz denial returns: HTTP 403 Content-Type: application/json {"error":{"type":"permission_denied","code":"RBAC_PERMISSION_DENIED","message":"You do not have permission to perform this action.","request_id":"<uuid>"}} - Protected route without permission metadata returns: HTTP 403 {"error":{"type":"permission_denied","code":"RBAC_MISSING_ROUTE_PERMISSION","message":"Access to this route is not configured.","request_id":"<uuid>"}} ## Implementation details - Introduced a RouteAuthzDescriptor that is attached at route registration time (permission list + scope resolver + “public/protected” marker). - Middleware extracts subject from the already-authenticated principal (user session / API key) and constructs an AuthzCheckRequest: subject_id, subject_type, org_id/project_id/env_id (as available), permission, resource_ref. - Evaluation is performed via PolicyEvaluatorClient (interface only in this PR; actual caching client lands in follow-up). - Added a small set of “scope resolvers” for gateway-known scopes (org-scoped API key management routes, org-scoped admin routes). Service-specific complex scope logic is intentionally deferred to service-level enforcement until the control plane annotations land. ## Changed areas / files - gateway/authz/middleware.ts: new authz middleware and mode gating (off/shadow/enforce) - gateway/routing/route_registry.ts: route metadata / descriptor plumbing - gateway/errors/rbac_errors.ts: standardized RBAC error payloads + codes - gateway/metrics/authz_metrics.ts: counters + histograms + tag set - gateway/config/flags.ts: RBAC_V2_GATEWAY_AUTHZ_MODE - gateway/tests/authz_middleware.test.ts: unit tests for allow/deny, missing metadata, and shadow mode - docs/internal/rbac-v2/gateway-enforcement.md: usage + how to tag routes (internal) ## Illustrative snippet (middleware) ```ts // pseudo from gateway/authz/middleware.ts export async function authzMiddleware(ctx, next) { const mode = flags.rbacV2GatewayAuthzMode(); if (mode === 'off') return next(); const desc = ctx.route.authz; if (!desc) { // route didn't opt into authz at all; treated as public for now return next(); } if (desc.visibility === 'public') return next(); if (!desc.permissions || desc.permissions.length === 0) { return deny(ctx, 'RBAC_MISSING_ROUTE_PERMISSION'); } const principal = ctx.principal; if (!principal) return deny(ctx, 'RBAC_SUBJECT_MISSING'); const scope = desc.resolveScope(ctx); const decision = await evaluator.check({ principal, scope, permissions: desc.permissions }); emitMetrics(decision, ctx, desc); if (mode === 'shadow') return next(); if (!decision.allow) return deny(ctx, 'RBAC_PERMISSION_DENIED'); return next(); } ``` ## Testing - Unit tests: decision allow/deny, deny-by-default for missing permissions, shadow mode does not block, metrics emitted, public allowlist unaffected. - Manual: verified /v1/orgs/:orgId/api-keys/* routes deny without appropriate permissions when mode=enforce using a low-privilege test principal. ## Rollout plan (follow-ups) 1) Land permission annotations for gateway-registered routes (separate PRs per area). 2) Enable shadow mode in staging + capture deny candidates and missing metadata. 3) Enable enforce mode for internal dogfood orgs; monitor deny rate + support tickets. 4) Gradually expand to pilot Private/Dedicated customers behind an org allowlist. ## Notes / risks - Deny-by-default can create hard fails if we flip enforce before metadata coverage is complete; shadow mode is intended to de-risk this. - This PR does not yet include user-facing denial “reason” details or debug headers (tracked separately); we keep responses stable and non-leaky for enterprise posture. - Service-level checks remain required for non-gateway entry points and for complex scope semantics; gateway enforcement is complementary, not a replacement. ## Review notes - Jordan: requested we separate RBAC_MISSING_ROUTE_PERMISSION from RBAC_PERMISSION_DENIED to make misconfiguration obvious during rollout; done. - Kaitlyn: asked to ensure we don’t change existing authn failures (401/403) and to avoid leaking permission names in responses; done. - Marcus: requested structured logs include org_id and subject_type for future audit correlation; added. ## Checklist - [x] Feature flag gated (off/shadow/enforce) - [x] Standardized JSON error format + stable codes - [x] Metrics + structured logs - [x] Unit tests - [x] Internal doc for route tagging ## CI - build: pass - lint: pass - unit: pass - gateway-contract-tests: pass ## Merge Merged via squash to main.
commits: gateway: add RouteAuthzDescriptor and registry plumbing
gateway: implement authz middleware with off/shadow/enforce modes
gateway: add authz metrics and structured logging fields
tests: add middleware unit tests and route fixtures
docs: internal notes for tagging protected routes
review_conversation: Jordan Lee (review): The deny-by-default behavior is good, but please make missing route permission metadata a distinct code from regular permission denied. That will be important during shadow rollout so we can distinguish “policy says no” vs “we forgot to annotate the route”.
Amara Diallo (author): +1. Added RBAC_MISSING_ROUTE_PERMISSION and updated tests + metrics tag to include denial_code.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): Can we confirm we’re not changing authn semantics? I don’t want this middleware to turn existing 401s into 403s or to block pre-auth routes accidentally. Also, please don’t return permission strings in the response payload.

Amara Diallo (author): Confirmed. Middleware is after principal resolution and only runs for routes marked protected. Public allowlist is explicit (/healthz, /readyz, auth bootstrap). Response payload uses stable codes only; permission names remain in logs only.
Marcus Lin (review): Please add structured log fields for org_id + subject_type and keep the response non-leaky. Also add a metric for shadow-mode denies so we can quantify impact before enforcement.
Amara Diallo (author): Added org_id, subject_type, route_name, and denial_code to logs. Added rbac_gateway_authz_shadow_denied_total metric and updated dashboards query snippet in internal doc.
Allison Grant (review): Metrics tag cardinality: avoid tagging on raw path (e.g., /orgs/:orgId/...). Use route_name not path. Also cap permission tags to a bounded set.
Amara Diallo (author): Updated to route_name and permission enum name (not free-form). No raw path tags.

Ethan Park (review): Looks good. One suggestion: ensure missing route metadata defaults to “public” only for now, but we should track follow-up to mark more routes protected. Approving since the protected routes in this PR are limited.
Amara Diallo (author): Agree. Added TODO in internal doc + linked ENG-18305 for coverage gating once control plane annotations land.
